benchmarks.title: One prompt through Cake and back
benchmarks.audience: A new Cake contributor who understands React but not the Electron/Pi seam.
benchmarks.goal: Trace one Project Session prompt from the composer to Pi and back to the visible transcript.
benchmarks.brief: Choose a composition that makes the outbound command and inbound live projection easy to follow. Do not imply that the renderer talks to Pi directly.

facts.claim: Chat renders a supplied ChatStore; ConversationSessionStore.chatStore wires submit to its ConversationComposerStore child.
ConversationSessionStore.deliver selects Client.sessionChats.prompt, or steer for an explicit steer; makeClient runs through Runtime and forwards AbortSignal.
CakeIpcClientLive maps the command to Effect RPC; preload exposes only frozen window.cake.rpc; the client protocol sends through that transport.
The main server protocol parses the request and adds trusted connection/correlation metadata; sessionChatHandlers binds the connection and calls sessionChats.deliver.
conversations.deliver dispatches to a scoped CakeSessionHandle and CakeSessionRuntimes.startTurn eventually calls the live runtime prompt.
createCakeSessionRuntime adapts Pi createAgentSession and events; ProjectSessions.observe and conversations.observe feed createModelObserver and applyProjectSessionUpdate on return.

relationships: Renderer commands use Client and validated RPC, not Pi or privileged implementations.
Main handlers adapt to domain operations; the domain acquires Pi capabilities.
Pi owns transcript/runtime facts; renderer Models and optimistic composer state are projections or temporary presentation state.
Observation starts with a current snapshot and continues with ordered events.
benchmarks.revisionScenario: Keep the end-to-end story, but select one turn and reveal accepted, streaming, and settled states while keeping the optimistic message renderer-local and Pi authority explicit.

benchmarks.title: Process and authority boundaries
benchmarks.goal: Distinguish renderer, preload, main, Pi, Cake domain/storage, and generated-code sandbox boundaries without inventing a web/server tier.
benchmarks.brief: Explain both privilege and authority. Show where code runs, where data is validated, and which system can reconstruct each durable fact after restart. Choose a boundary treatment rather than assuming a node-and-edge map.

facts.claim: main.ts creates the process ManagedRuntime from makeMainLive and starts MainApplication; makeMainLive composes storage, native, Pi, session workflows, workers, and RPC in main.
Renderer bootstrap creates one window Runtime, Client, RootProjection, and Store tree, then attaches observers and persistence; makeRuntime keeps ManagedRuntime private.
Preload exposes only frozen rpc through contextBridge and has no Cake business logic or general Electron API.
Both transport sides decode messages; the main server routes responses to the originating webContents and RendererConnectionMiddlewareLive supplies trusted connection/correlation context.
The source-of-truth table assigns Project Session transcripts/tool history/branching/compaction to Pi, application/workflow/artifact metadata to Cake, and renderer Models to validated projections.
compileInlineWidget restricts generated source, handleInlineWidgetScheme serves a CSP-limited document, and WidgetArtifact runs it in an allow-scripts iframe with tokenized messages.

relationships: Privileged filesystem, native Electron, storage, Cake domain, and Pi work remain in main; renderer access crosses the validated bridge.
Preload is mechanical transport, not an authority layer.
Pi owns transcript/runtime facts, Cake owns application/artifact metadata, and renderer Models are derived projections.
Generated React/SVG runs without Cake, Node, Electron, filesystem, parent-DOM, or arbitrary network/API privileges; CSP media allowances are the only remote-resource exception.
benchmarks.revisionScenario: Make the renderer Model visibly a projection rather than a database. Move widget CSP and token details into an optional security disclosure while retaining the no-privilege iframe boundary and its documented media allowances.

benchmarks.title: Dense delegated-widget dependency case
benchmarks.audience: A specialist implementing an interactive explanation and a reviewer checking its seams.
benchmarks.goal: Explain the existing delegated-widget path from a primary Pi request through isolated generation, compile/repair, artifact persistence, and sandboxed display. This is not a claim that the new automatic workflow is shipped.
benchmarks.brief: Keep brief/data/fallback and security constraints primary. Choose a composition suited to dependency density; a graph is allowed but not required, and do not expose source code or coordinates just to represent the dependencies.

facts.claim: The widgets.present definition accepts bounded brief/data/fallback, calls generateInlineWidget with model and turn signal, persists a cake.artifact/v1 widget, and appends a Pi artifact pointer.

ProjectSessionIntegrationHost.generateInlineWidget extracts one cake-react result, compile-checks it, and on compile failure runs repair with diagnostic/context before compiling repaired source; persistArtifact emits artifact-updated after upsert.
Widget generation/repair use runIsolatedSession with projectTrusted false and noTools all; the resource loader disables extensions, skills, prompt templates, themes, and context files.

compileInlineWidget enforces a 1 MiB source limit and React/approved-D3 imports; the tokenized document CSP defaults to no sources and permits only explicit inline script/style and data/HTTPS media cases.
WidgetArtifact uses InlineWidgetStore for compile/repair, renders sandbox allow-scripts, validates tokenized postMessage events, and can place the widget in FullscreenSurface.

ArtifactRepository.upsert validates, content-addresses, writes immutable blobs, and requires one-step revisions; retaining a prior successful published artifact after a failed revision is production-phase policy, not a prototype result.

relationships: The primary Pi session supplies brief/data/fallback, not privileged generated code.
Repair receives source/diagnostics as untrusted data and must not widen tools, imports, frame privileges, or arbitrary network/API access.
Cake owns published artifact metadata, Pi owns the transcript pointer, and the iframe owns only local presentation runtime.
A failed revision is not a successful publication; prior-success retention is deferred to production until atomic publication is implemented.
benchmarks.revisionScenario: Keep the main composition, but make the compile/repair boundary inspectable, explain why repaired source remains sandboxed, and preserve the previous successful published revision if the requested revision fails. The final retention clause is production-phase.
